stops.opening: Your ride is running 15 minutes late. You were supposed to set out the craft bins by 8:30.
choices: Text Kai: "Ride's late, here by 8:45. Can someone set out the craft bins?"
Kai texts back: 'Thanks for telling me. I've got the bins.'
Say nothing and hurry in when you get there.
You arrive at 8:45. Dev is doing sign-in alone and setting out bins at the same time.
Kai texts back: 'How late? Anything I need to cover?' Your ride pulls in before you answer.

stops.opening: Mia wants to use the hot glue gun herself.
choices: Explain the rule, then let Mia point where every dot of glue goes while you hold the gun.
Mia directs every dot. Her owl ends up with three eyes, on purpose.
Let her try it just this once while you watch.
Mia is careful. Two other Bluebirds were watching.
Say no and move on to the next camper.
Mia folds her arms and stops working on her owl.

stops.opening: You count the Bluebirds. Seven. There should be eight.
choices: Stop the line, count again, and radio Kai.
Leo was tying his shoe by the fountain. Kai walks him up. You reach the pool three minutes late, and the lifeguard counts eight.
At the pool the lifeguard counts seven. Kai runs back and finds Leo by the fountain, scared.
Ask Dev to walk the group on while you run back to look.
You find Leo at the fountain. But Dev walked seven kids to the pool alone, and the lifeguard noticed.

stops.opening: A juice box bursts across a whole table. Dev is on his phone.
choices: Ask Dev straight out: "Can you grab paper towels? I'll move the kids."
Dev jumps up. 'Sorry, my mom texted.' The table is dry in two minutes.
Clean it all yourself and complain to Kai later.
It takes you ten minutes. Kai says she'll talk to Dev.
Post "Dev is useless lol" in the junior counselor group chat.
Three people react with laughing faces. Dev sees it.

stops.opening: It's too hot for running games. Ms. Ortega asks the junior counselors for an idea.
choices: Suggest a shade game you know and offer to explain it.
Ms. Ortega says, 'Great. Go.' Eight kids learn a new game in the shade.
Say you don't have any ideas.
Ms. Ortega picks a game herself. It's fine.
Suggest letting the campers vote between two shade games.
The vote takes one minute, and everyone plays the winner.

stops.opening: Thunder. Everyone heads inside, but the Otters group is already in the gym.
choices: Find Ms. Ortega and tell her both groups are at the gym.
Ms. Ortega opens the art room. 'Thanks for coming to me instead of fighting it out.'
Tell the Otters' counselor the gym is yours today.
The two of you argue in front of sixteen kids until Kai steps in.
Take the Bluebirds to the hallway for a quiet game without telling anyone.
Kai checks the gym, then the art room, then finds you. 'I didn't know where my group was.'

stops.opening: Mr. Price asks how Leo's day went.
choices: Tell him one thing Leo did today, like finding the shady spot for the game.
Mr. Price grins. 'He never tells me anything. Thanks.'
Mr. Price nods and heads off.
Ms. Ortega answers him, and wonders why you didn't.
problemChoices: Listen first, then tell him plainly what happened and offer to get Ms. Ortega.
Mr. Price nods. 'Thanks for being straight with me.' Ms. Ortega talks with him.
Say none of it was your fault.
Mr. Price asks for Ms. Ortega, and he is not happy.
Mr. Price frowns. That night he hears the whole story from Leo.

stops.opening: Ms. Ortega asks each junior counselor: what will you do differently tomorrow?
choices: Name one thing you'd change and one you'd keep.
She writes it down. 'That's how you get better at this.'
She waits a moment, then moves on to Dev.
Ask her advice about your hardest moment today.
She tells you about her first summer, when she lost a whole group for five minutes.

arrivals.heads_up: The bins are out and the glue guns are warm.
arrivals.silent: Craft starts ten minutes late, and two campers never got signed in.
arrivals.vague: Kai set out half the bins. The glitter is missing.
arrivals.asked_dev: Dev nudges you: 'Say the shadow tag one.'
arrivals.posted: Dev sits at the far end of the bench.
arrivals.flat_no: Mia is still sulking from craft time.
arrivals.bent_rule: On the way in, a Bluebird grabs a glue gun from the craft cart. 'Mia got to!' Kai takes it away.
arrivals.kept_walking: Leo told his dad he got left behind at the fountain. Mr. Price is upset.
arrivals.split_up: Leo told his dad you ran back to find him. Mr. Price wants to know what happened.
arrivals.silent_pickup: Mr. Price asks why Leo's sign-in sheet has no time on it.

kai.heads_up: You told me early, so I could cover. That's most of this job.
kai.silent: I didn't know you'd be late. Dev did two jobs this morning.
kai.vague: Next time, tell me what needs covering, not just that you're late.
kai.bent_rule: One of ours grabbed a glue gun because Mia got to use one.
kai.told_director: The art room save was smart.
kai.argued: Arguing over the gym in front of the kids didn't help anyone.
kai.vanished: When I can't find my group, my stomach drops. Radio me first.

dev.asked_dev: Thanks for just asking me. I'm putting my phone away tomorrow.
dev.complained: I wish you'd told me yourself instead of Kai.

ortega.safe_way: Mia showed me her three-eyed owl.
ortega.stopped_count: You stopped the line to count. That's exactly right.
ortega.kept_walking: Counting is the job. We were lucky today.
ortega.split_up: You found Leo. Next time radio first, so no one is alone with a group.
ortega.led_idea: Your shade game was a hit.
ortega.honest: Parents trust us when we're straight with them.
ortega.specific: Parents trust us when we're straight with them.
ortega.blamed: Owning it would have helped with Mr. Price.
ortega.smoothed: Mr. Price called me tonight. Tell parents what really happened.
ortega.fine: Parents love one real detail about their kid.
ortega.passed_on: Parents love one real detail about their kid.
ortega.shrug: Think about one thing for tomorrow. See you at 8:30.
